title: From the TRS-80 to “the ’80s called”
lede: Two commercials from the Tandy years, a 1991 television episode about the company’s computers, the Super Bowl spot that made fun of its own stores, the news from the day of the bankruptcy, and a later look back.

videos.title: “The ’80s called,” the Super Bowl XLVIII spot
videos.caption: Aired February 2, 2014: 1980s characters arrive to take an old-style RadioShack store back.[^24] This 72-second cut was uploaded by a viewer on the day of the game. Chapter 11 followed a year later.[^15]

videos.title: Radio Shack introduces the TRS-80
videos.caption: A 30-second spot for Tandy’s own personal computer, sold through the stores. The 1978 date comes from the uploader; we could not confirm when it aired.

videos.title: “You’ve got questions. We’ve got answers.”: cellular phones
videos.caption: The service slogan, attached to the product line that would be about half of sales by 2013.[^13] According to the uploader it was recorded on September 22, 1995 from WJBK in Detroit. The trademark was still among the assets sold in 2020.[^28]

videos.title: Computer Chronicles: “Tandy / Radio Shack Computers”
videos.caption: A full episode of the television series, first broadcast in 1991, on the role Radio Shack played in early personal computing. A Tandy vice president is a guest and the original TRS-80 is shown.[^37]

videos.title: CNBC: “RadioShack Files for Chapter 11 Bankruptcy”
videos.caption: A one-minute report posted by CNBC on February 6, 2015, the day after the filing in Delaware.[^15]

videos.title: The Dallas Morning News: “RadioShack declares bankruptcy”
videos.caption: The home-town paper’s business columnist and a business writer discuss the filing, posted on February 5, 2015. RadioShack was run from Fort Worth.[^18]

videos.title: Company Man: “The Decline of RadioShack...What Happened?”
videos.caption: A fourteen-minute independent retrospective published in August 2017, after the second bankruptcy. Its figures are the uploader’s; ours are in the sections above.

note: Video titles and upload dates are as shown by the host. Where a commercial’s year comes only from the uploader, the caption says so.
